Question: Forwarder (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a component installed on a data source that collects data and sends it to an indexer.

Question: Indexer (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the component that processes incoming data and stores it in indexes so it can be searched.

Question: Search head (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the component that hosts the web interface, takes searches and gathers results from indexers.

Question: Index (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a repository where Splunk stores data in a searchable form.

Question: Event (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a single record of machine data, usually one log entry, with a timestamp.

Question: App (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a packaged set of configuration and content, such as dashboards and searches, for a particular purpose.

Question: Search & Reporting (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the default app that holds the search bar, reports, alerts and dashboards.

Question: Role (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a set of capabilities and index access assigned to a user.

Question: Time range picker (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the control beside the search bar that sets the window of time a search covers.

Question: Timeline (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the bar chart above the events showing how many matched in each slice of time.

Question: Fields sidebar (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the panel listing fields found in search results, split into selected and interesting.

Question: Search job (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the process Splunk creates each time a search runs, which can be paused, stopped, shared or inspected.

Question: Search mode (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the setting (fast, smart or verbose) that trades speed against how many fields are discovered.

Question: host (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a default field naming the machine that produced the event.

Question: source (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a default field naming the file, port or script an event came from.

Question: sourcetype (basics and basic searching)
Answer: a default field naming the format or type of the data.

Question: Wildcard (basics and basic searching)
Answer: an asterisk in a search term that matches any run of characters.

Question: Snap to (basics and basic searching)
Answer: the @ time modifier syntax that rounds a time boundary to the start of a unit.

Question: Be specific early (fields and search language)
Answer: index, sourcetype and a narrow time range first.

Question: Field (fields and search language)
Answer: a name and value extracted from an event so it can be searched and calculated on.

Question: Default fields (fields and search language)
Answer: fields Splunk adds to every event at index time, such as host, source, sourcetype, index, _time and _raw.

Question: Selected fields (fields and search language)
Answer: fields displayed with each event in the results, host, source and sourcetype by default.

Question: Interesting fields (fields and search language)
Answer: fields that appear in a substantial share of the events in the current results.

Question: Search-time extraction (fields and search language)
Answer: pulling field values from event text when the search runs rather than when data is indexed.

Question: Field comparison (fields and search language)
Answer: a search term of the form fieldname=value, where names are case sensitive and values are not.

Question: IN operator (fields and search language)
Answer: a shorthand that matches a field against a list of values.

Question: Pipe (fields and search language)
Answer: the vertical bar that passes the output of one search command to the next.

Question: Streaming command (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that works on each event as it passes through, such as eval, rename or fields.

Question: Transforming command (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that turns events into a table of statistics, such as stats, top or rare.

Question: table (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that shows the named fields as columns in the order given.

Question: rename (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that gives a field a new name using AS.

Question: fields (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that keeps (plus) or removes (minus) fields from the results.

Question: dedup (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that removes events repeating the value of the named field, keeping the first.

Question: sort (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that orders results, with a minus sign meaning descending.

Question: head (fields and search language)
Answer: a command that keeps the first N results.

Question: Transforming command (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that converts events into a table of statistics.

Question: Results table (transforming commands)
Answer: the rows and columns a transforming command produces, shown on the Statistics tab.

Question: top (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that returns the most common values of a field with count and percent.

Question: rare (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that returns the least common values of a field with count and percent.

Question: stats (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that calculates statistics over events, optionally grouped with by.

Question: count (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that returns the number of events.

Question: dc (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that returns the number of distinct values of a field.

Question: sum (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that totals numeric values.

Question: avg (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that returns the mean of numeric values.

Question: values (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that returns the distinct values of a field as a sorted list.

Question: list (transforming commands)
Answer: a stats function that returns every value of a field in order, duplicates included.

Question: by clause (transforming commands)
Answer: the part of a stats, top or rare command that groups results by one or more fields.

Question: limit (transforming commands)
Answer: a top and rare argument that sets how many values are returned, with zero meaning all.

Question: chart (transforming commands)
Answer: a command like stats designed to produce data for a chart with an x-axis field.

Question: timechart (transforming commands)
Answer: a command like chart that always uses time as the x-axis.

Question: eventstats (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that adds statistics to each event as a new field instead of replacing events.

Question: where (transforming commands)
Answer: a command that filters results with an expression, comparing strings case sensitively.

Question: Private (reports and dashboards)
Answer: only the owner sees it.

Question: Edit Description (reports and dashboards)
Answer: Edit Permissions

Question: Column, bar, line, area (reports and dashboards)
Answer: comparing values or showing trends. Line and area charts are the usual choice for values over time.

Question: Pie (reports and dashboards)
Answer: showing proportion of a whole for a small number of categories.

Question: Scatter and bubble (reports and dashboards)
Answer: relationship between numeric fields.

Question: Single value (reports and dashboards)
Answer: one prominent number, optionally with a trend indicator.

Question: Report (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a saved search together with its presentation settings, re-run when opened.

Question: Save As (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the menu on the search page for saving a search as a report, alert, dashboard panel or event type.

Question: Reports page (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the page in the app navigation that lists saved reports and lets you edit them.

Question: Permissions (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the owner, app and role settings that decide who can read or write a saved object.

Question: Visualization (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a chart, gauge, single value, map or similar graphical presentation of a results table.

Question: Format menu (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the control that changes how a table or chart looks without changing the search.

Question: Drilldown (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the behavior when a viewer clicks part of a table or chart, usually running a more specific search.

Question: Dashboard (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a page of panels that show visualizations or tables built from searches and reports.

Question: Panel (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a single block on a dashboard that displays one search result.

Question: Input (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a dashboard control such as a time picker or dropdown that lets viewers change the data shown.

Question: Token (reports and dashboards)
Answer: a placeholder in a dashboard that an input fills with a value.

Question: Dashboard Studio (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the newer Splunk dashboard builder with a canvas and a JSON definition.

Question: Simple XML (reports and dashboards)
Answer: the XML format that defines classic dashboards.

Question: Report acceleration (reports and dashboards)
Answer: stored precomputed summaries that make a frequently run report faster.

Question: Lookup (lookups)
Answer: a table of values that Splunk consults at search time to add fields to events.

Question: File-based lookup (lookups)
Answer: a lookup stored as a CSV file uploaded to Splunk.

Question: KV Store lookup (lookups)
Answer: a lookup stored in a database-like collection that searches and apps can update.

Question: External lookup (lookups)
Answer: a lookup whose values come from a script Splunk runs.

Question: Input field (lookups)
Answer: the lookup column matched against a field in the event.

Question: Output field (lookups)
Answer: a lookup column whose value is added to matching events.

Question: Lookup table file (lookups)
Answer: the uploaded CSV that holds the lookup data.

Question: Lookup definition (lookups)
Answer: a named configuration that points at a lookup source and sets rules for using it.

Question: lookup command (lookups)
Answer: the search command that applies a lookup definition to events.

Question: OUTPUT (lookups)
Answer: the lookup argument that adds output fields and overwrites existing fields of the same name.

Question: OUTPUTNEW (lookups)
Answer: the lookup argument that adds output fields only where the field is absent.

Question: inputlookup (lookups)
Answer: a generating command that returns the rows of a lookup as search results.

Question: outputlookup (lookups)
Answer: a command that writes search results into a lookup file.

Question: Automatic lookup (lookups)
Answer: a lookup configured to apply to every event of a sourcetype, source or host without a lookup command.

Question: Enrichment (lookups)
Answer: adding meaning to events from outside the event, such as names for identifiers.

Question: Schedule Report (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: tick to turn scheduling on.

Question: Schedule (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: how often. Common choices are every hour, every day, every week, every month, or a cron schedule, a five-field expression for precise timing (for example, minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week).

Question: Time Range (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: the window of data each run covers, such as the last 24 hours. Note that this is separate from the schedule: running every hour over the last 24 hours is legitimate.

Question: Schedule Priority (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: how important the run is when the system is busy.

Question: Schedule Window (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a period during which Splunk may start the run late if the system is loaded, which helps spread out many reports scheduled for the same moment.

Question: Trigger Actions (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: what to do when the report runs. For a scheduled report the usual actions are to send an email, run a script or log an event.

Question: Custom (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a condition you write as a search expression on the results.

Question: Add to Triggered Alerts (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: records the alert in a list inside Splunk.

Question: Send email (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: to named recipients, with a subject and message, optionally including the results.

Question: Run a script (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: execute a script on the Splunk server.

Question: Webhook (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: send an HTTP POST to a URL, used to notify chat tools and ticket systems.

Question: Scheduled report (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a report set to run automatically on a timetable.

Question: Cron schedule (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a time expression with minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week fields for precise scheduling.

Question: Alert (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a saved search that triggers actions when its results meet a condition.

Question: Scheduled alert (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: an alert that runs on a timetable over a set time range.

Question: Real-time alert (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: an alert whose search runs continuously on live data.

Question: Per-result trigger (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a real-time or scheduled setting that fires the alert once for every matching result.

Question: Trigger condition (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: the rule, such as number of results greater than a value, that decides whether an alert fires.

Question: Throttling (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: suppressing repeat alerts for a set period after one has fired.

Question: Trigger action (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: something an alert does when it fires, such as sending email or calling a webhook.

Question: Severity (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: a label from info to critical attached to a fired alert.

Question: Triggered alerts list (scheduled reports and alerts)
Answer: the page that shows when alerts fired and lets you view their results.
